info.name: QA-Demo Project
info.description:
Purpose:
Professional API testing collection for the QA-Demo application.

Application:
https://qademo.com/

Current Phase:
Phase 4 - API Test Automation

API definitions:
Derived from Phase 2 API Discovery (docs/API_DISCOVERY.md, docs/api-inventory.json). All requests, methods, headers, and bodies in this collection reflect only what was actually discovered/verified - nothing is invented.

API Base URL:
https://qademo.com/api (environment variable {{apiUrl}})

Authentication:
Bearer access token (Authorization: Bearer {{authToken}}) for user/admin-protected endpoints, obtained from POST /auth/login. Cart endpoints instead require an X-Session-ID header ({{sessionId}}), independent of login state.

Test automation (Phase 4):
All 24 Phase 3 requests now carry request-level pm.test() assertions covering status codes, response time, Content-Type, response structure, required fields, data types, and (where the API is stateless/public) request/response consistency. A collection-level test enforces a 3000ms response-time budget on every request. Endpoints whose authenticated success response could not be observed live (no test credentials were available) use conditional assertions that validate the currently-reproducible unauthenticated/error path exactly, and validate only the presence of a plausible success shape if a token is later supplied - see docs/API_TEST_AUTOMATION.md.

A new '07 - Negative Tests' folder holds 14 dedicated, deterministic negative/boundary requests (missing/invalid fields, invalid types, unknown ids, boundary quantity values, missing auth) verified live during Phase 4 - some are new findings not previously captured in Phase 2 (e.g. cart quantity must be > 0 on add, >= 0 on update).

Three endpoints (POST /products, PATCH /products/{id}, POST /orders) still have a verified method/URL/auth requirement but an undetermined request body schema - see docs/POSTMAN_IMPLEMENTATION.md. Their tests validate only the authentication requirement.

No dynamic data chaining (auto-populating tokens/ids between requests) has been implemented - that is Phase 5.

Future phases:
Phase 5 - Data Chaining
Phase 6 - Newman
Phase 7 - Git/GitHub
Phase 8 - GitHub Actions / CI/CD

item.name: 01 - Authentication
item.description: Login, logout, token refresh, and current-user endpoints. Verified in Phase 2 API discovery (docs/API_DISCOVERY.md, section 'Authentication').

request.description:
Purpose:
Log in with a username and password.

Method:
POST

Endpoint:
/auth/login

Authentication:
Not required.

Parameters:
None.

Body (required, JSON):
{ "username": string, "password": string } - both required (verified live via Zod validation error when omitted).

Expected response:
200 - { success: true, data: { accessToken, user } } (inferred, not observed live - no valid credentials were available during discovery).
401 - { success: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_CREDENTIALS', message } } (verified live).
400 - Zod validation error, wrapped in the standard error envelope: { success: false, error: { issues: [...], name: 'ZodError' } } when required fields are missing (verified live; corrected in Phase 4 - Phase 2/3 had documented this as a top-level, unwrapped shape).

Note: on a successful login, manually copy the returned accessToken into the `authToken` environment variable to use the authenticated requests in this collection. Automated token chaining is planned for Phase 5.

exec: try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }

pm.test("400 response is a ZodError with an issues array", function () {
pm.test("Status code is 401 for invalid credentials", function () {
pm.test("401 response uses the standard error envelope", function () {
pm.test("Status code is 200 for successful login", function () {
pm.test("Successful login returns success=true and an accessToken", function () {
pm.test("Login returned an undocumented status code (" + status + ")", function () {
pm.expect.fail("Undocumented status code from POST /auth/login: " + status);

request.description:
Purpose:
Exchange a refresh token (cookie) for a new access token.

Method:
POST

Endpoint:
/auth/refresh

Authentication:
None via header - relies on a same-origin cookie set during login (the frontend sends every request with credentials: "include"). Postman will send/receive cookies for this domain automatically if 'Send cookies' is enabled and a prior login was performed in the same session/cookie jar.

Parameters:
None.

Body:
None (no request body is sent by the frontend client).

Expected response:
200 - { success: true, data: { accessToken } } (inferred, not observed live).
401 if no valid refresh cookie is present.

Note: refresh-token cookie attributes (name, httpOnly, Secure, SameSite, expiry) could not be determined in Phase 2 - no successful login was performed. See docs/API_DISCOVERY.md, Discovery Limitations.

exec: pm.test("Status code is 401 without a valid refresh cookie", function () {
pm.test("401 response uses the standard error envelope", function () {
pm.test("Status code is 200 when a valid refresh cookie is present", function () {
pm.test("Successful refresh returns a new accessToken", function () {
pm.test("Refresh Token returned an undocumented status code (" + status + ")", function () {
pm.expect.fail("Undocumented status code from POST /auth/refresh: " + status);

item.name: 08 - Cleanup
item.description: Reserved for future phases. Delete/clear operations for resources actually created during test runs (e.g. deleting a test product, clearing a test cart) already exist as individual requests in their respective resource folders (02 - Products, 03 - Cart). Phase 5 (Data Chaining) will sequence create -> use -> cleanup flows; this folder remains empty until then.

item.name: 09 - Workflows
item.description: Phase 5 - API Data Chaining & Workflow Automation. Each sub-folder is an ordered, chained workflow using pm.execution.setNextRequest() to connect dependent requests, with dynamic data extraction/storage via pm.collectionVariables and pm.environment (no hardcoded generated IDs). Run a sub-folder with the Collection Runner (select only that sub-folder, or run it standalone starting from its first request) to execute the full chain in order. These workflows are additive - they do not modify the original Phase 3/4 requests in folders 01-08, whose Phase 4 assertions remain fully intact. See docs/API_DATA_CHAINING.md for the full architecture, variable strategy, and known limitations.

item.name: Workflow 01 - Authentication Chaining
item.description: Login -> capture accessToken -> authenticated request. Requires valid credentials in {{username}}/{{password}} to reach step 2 - see Known Limitations in docs/API_DATA_CHAINING.md.
